thread.title: Tencent Music IPO: Good News For Tencent, Bad News For The Stock Market - Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME)

author: David Evans
title: Tencent Music IPO: Good News For Tencent, Bad News For The Stock Market - Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE:TME)
text:
Tencent Music (NYSE: TME ), the music streaming section of Chinese tech giant Tencent Holding ( OTCPK:TCEHY ) (HKG:0700), has released details about its IPO. The Street has reported that Tencent “has filed papers to raise between $1.07 billion and $1.23 billion” on the NYSE, by selling 82 million American depository receipts at a price between $13 to $15. Tencent has reportedly targeted a valuation between $22 to $25 billion, making it the third largest Chinese IPO in 2018.
Tencent Holding itself has struggled mightily over the past year and Chinese IPOs have not performed well in 2018. However, the company’s financial numbers appear to be extremely solid and it has plenty of room to grow. But even if its streaming service, Tencent Music, performs well on its IPO, the timing of this IPO is very strange and portends that next year’s IPO market could be more unstable.
Examining Tencent Tencent Holding's stock has dropped by over 24% in the last year due to new Chinese regulations against its games and online direct lenders, but this is only tangentially related to Tencent Music’s operations. Tencent Music has been frequently compared to Spotify (NYSE: SPOT ) or Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) Music, as a streaming platform for music. In its SEC report , Tencent declares that it is “the largest online music entertainment platform in China, operating the top four music mobile apps in terms of mobile MAUs in the third quarter of 2018.” Tencent claims a staggering 800 million unique MAUs, though only 3.6 percent of them are paying users.
It should be noted that the 800 million figure almost certainly does not represent the true number of Tencent’s users. Many users will have multiple accounts for a variety of reasons such as double dipping on certain promotional deals, and a substantial amount of those accounts are likely bots.
But regardless of the true number, there is little doubt that Tencent has a huge amount of users, and we know that the Chinese music market will continue to increase. Tencent Music claims that its forecasts predict that the Chinese online market for music will have a CAGR of 36.7% from 2017 to 2023, and even less optimistic and perhaps more realistic predictions forecast high, double-digit growth over the coming years. These results could be even higher if China cracks down on problems such as rampant music piracy.
On top of those good news, this company has extremely strong financials. Tencent Music’s revenue increased from 7.4 billion RMB in the first three quarters of 2017 to 13.6 billion RMB ($1.9 billion) in the same 2018 time frame. The company has also managed to stay profitable, and also reports having $1.7 billion cash on hand compared to just $811 million in total liabilities. In summation, Tencent appears to be a fantastic company with strong financial numbers and major growth prospects, and so would initially appear to be an obvious investment.
The Problem Of Timing But while there is a lot to like about Tencent, a reasonable question is why is it going for an IPO now? IPOs rarely file in December, with The New York Times reporting that only three companies with a valuation of more than $1 billion have filed for a December IPO in the past decade. And Tencent is not in a position now where it needs to go for an IPO now to fix some financial problem.
Tencent Music appears to have gone for an IPO now because it is convinced that the window to file for a successful IPO may be soon closing. The company had originally planned to launch its IPO in mid-October according to Reuters , but delayed it due to recent jitters in the stock market. The fact that President Trump and China announced a truce on their trade war likely serves as a major impetus for Tencent’s decision to launch now.
But no one seriously thinks that Trump and China are done fighting with each other over trade, and there have bee continued concerns about a Chinese economic slowdown for reasons beyond a trade war. The Chinese market has room to further grow, but Tencent’s decision to go for an IPO now should be a red flag for investors, especially those who are less trusting towards Chinese numbers.
It should also be noted that despite Tencent Music’s good numbers, the valuation is rather high. If we assume a midpoint market cap of $23.5 billion and divide by its 2017 revenue of $1.6 billion, we are looking at a P/S ratio of 14.7. By comparison, Spotify has a P/S ratio of 4.2 and peaked at 6.4 in late July.
Cautious Optimism Or Just Caution? By the standards of a Chinese IPO, Tencent is an excellent company with strong financials and potential for growth. But investors have legitimate reasons to be concerned about the past performance of other Chinese IPOs, its peculiar timing, as well as a higher valuation compared to its competitors.
Nevertheless, I would argue that Tencent can still be a solid investment at the IPO price of $13 to $15. But if the company makes a huge post-IPO jump as other investors chase Chinese growth, do not follow the crowd. Wait for the stock to go down in value, and consider putting it in your portfolio depending on the state of the economy and more importantly relations between China and the United States.
